Denver is suspending its popular electric bike incentive program.
The program was launched in April.
It allowed Denver residents to apply for $400 in government funds before buying an electric bike from a participating shop.
Residents who met certain income qualifications could qualify for $1,200.
The city then changed the program to limit the number of applications each month.
On Monday, the city announced the pause.
The city expects to resume the program early next year.
It also plans design changes to make participation easier and increase access to the program.

However, research indicates that this is not actually the case.
What consumers really think or feel often contradicts what they say.
A big reason is that they are driven by unconscious urges, the biggest of which is emotion.
Emotion is what really drives the purchasing behaviors and also decision-making in general.
Good marketers keep in mind this important fact all the time.
And examples of emotion-based campaigns are everywhere.
Think for a moment, what is actually being sold in most marketing campaigns?
Luxury goods target our feelings of self-worth, acceptance, and status in the world.
Communication devices excite us by offering a connection to friends, family, and a broader network of people.
And many other products, such as rings, target emotions related to love and relationships.
As marketers, we should focus on the features of the product, but we must also sell the lifestyle and the feeling.
The key is to highlight the emotional response a consumer will have by using the product.
To achieve the highest emotional response, we should target our consumer through many different senses.
A lot of what drives consumers is subconscious behavior.
But this isn't a bad thing.
There's nothing manipulative about helping consumers achieve desired states of emotion.

55% said they owned at least one pet.
Dogs were the most common pet, followed by cats.
But whatever the type of animal, the vast majority of owners said their pets boosted their mental and physical health.
Roughly 80% said their pets reduced stress, and almost three quarters said their pets provided a sense of purpose.
However, people did report a few disadvantages to pet ownership.
These included difficulty traveling and financial strains.
Still, plenty of research has shown that just about anyone can benefit from their pet since animals can lower stress, reduce symptoms of depression and anxiety, and encourage physical activity.
The new poll suggests that pet ownership may be especially beneficial for older adults, given how common loneliness and social isolation are within this age group.
Human social support comes with a host of health benefits: less stress, lower rates of long-term disease, and more.
And research shows that interacting with pets can bring many of the same benefits.
